_purpose: Reviewed differences between the committed special-instrument closes (rates / vol / commodities / fx in data/weekly and data/daily) and the provider's own history, as scripts/audit_instruments.py found them. An entry is a statement that the difference was looked at, not that it was fixed: the files are observations and are never edited (DATA_FEED.md sec.1). 'committed' is what the file holds, 'provider' is the provider's bar dated as_of when the audit ran, and 'session' is the session whose close the committed number actually is, where it is one.
_regenerate: python scripts/audit_instruments.py --write   (replaces 'audited' and 'findings', keeps everything else, and carries a finding's cause forward only while the finding is unchanged; review what is NEW first and give it a cause here by hand)

_classes.prior_session: the as_of bar exists and the committed close is the session before it
_classes.holiday_stand_in: no as_of bar for the instrument; the committed close is the last session of the same Mon..Fri week
_classes.other_session: the close of a different nearby session
_classes.differs: no session's close: restated since, read before settlement, or another contract month
_classes.absent: no close in the file; the provider has a bar dated as_of
_classes.unverified: the provider could not answer; never an ok

index_bar_absent_at_fetch.what: 2026-08-28.json holds the 2026-08-27 close for its three index instruments.
index_bar_absent_at_fetch.evidence: Fetched 2026-08-29T14:10:48Z. US10Y 4.672, VIX 14.51 and DXY 99.16 are the provider's closes for the 27th; its closes for the 28th are 4.72, 14.43 and 99.7. All three are Yahoo INDEX-type symbols (^TNX, ^VIX, DX-Y.NYB) and the futures in the same file are Friday's, so the provider had not posted Friday's index bars by then, or served a copy of Thursday's; the file cannot say which. macro/facts.json generated later that day already carried 4.72 and 14.43. Cboe's own VIX history gives 14.51 and 14.43, and the Treasury par curve gives the 10-year as 4.67 and 4.73. The dollar index has no second source. Effect while it stood: US10Y d1w -7 bp where it was -2, then +11 where it was +6; DXY d1w 0.0 on 2026-09-04 where it was -0.5, and d4w +1.9 on 2026-09-25 where it was +1.3.
index_bar_absent_at_fetch.resolution: Corrected, owner sign-off 2026-10-05: 2026-08-28.corrected.json restates the three closes, each labelled yahoo-backfill in provenance. The original is unchanged and stays listed here, superseded. The writer no longer takes an earlier bar unless a later one proves the date was skipped.

untraded_mark_not_posted_yet.what: rates.US2Y is the previous session's mark.
untraded_mark_not_posted_yet.evidence: 2YY=F is not traded (volume 0 on 51 of 54 sessions); its daily value is an exchange mark posted at settlement. Read on the evening of the session the bar still held the prior day's: weekly 2026-09-11, 09-18 and 09-25 hold 4.375, 4.404 and 4.472 against 4.380, 4.416 and 4.500, and seven of the eight daily files written by the evening job are the same (2026-09-22, a day the contract traded, is right).
untraded_mark_not_posted_yet.resolution: Panel left as written. Nothing derives from these any more: since 2026-10-04 market_state reads the Treasury 2-year (DATA_FEED.md sec.1a). The future is committed as US2Y_FUT, and the writer now reads it only after it has settled.

holiday_stand_in_unmarked.what: A holiday Friday's instrument is the last session of its week, and the file does not say so per instrument.
holiday_stand_in_unmarked.evidence: Five files, 28 instruments: 2025-04-18, 2026-04-03, 2026-06-19 and 2026-07-03 hold the Thursday close for all six instruments listed, and 2025-07-04 for four. Each file carries a file-level session_note ('Friday holiday; bars from <Thursday>'), which is about the equity series. In 2025-07-04.json it is wrong for part of the file: WTI and SILVER are from the July 4 holiday session's own bar, and US10Y, US2Y, VIX and DXY from July 3. The writer attached a note to each stand-in and snapshot._normalize_block dropped it.
holiday_stand_in_unmarked.resolution: Panel left as written; the values are what the holiday rule produces. The session each one belongs to is the 'session' of its finding here. New files record it in provenance.<block>.<ticker>.observed.

gold_series_rebuilt.what: The committed GOLD is a different contract month from the one the provider's GC=F history now carries for the date.
gold_series_rebuilt.evidence: 104 weeks. The committed close is always lower, by 0.50 to 59.00 (at most 1.67 percent), and on thin volume: median 491 contracts, under 10,000 in 102 of the 104, against a median of 185,701 in the provider's history today. That is the nearest-expiry contract against the active one, and the difference is the carry between them: it shrinks week by week, is zero on the four Fridays the nearest-expiry contract WAS the active one (2024-11-29, 2025-01-31, 2025-03-28, 2025-05-30), then jumps to the next spread. From 2026-07-31 the provider's GC=F rows are GCZ26.CMX's, close and volume, row for row, and a window as short as the writer's returns the same rows as the full history. Of the live files, 2026-08-14, 08-21 and 09-04 are on the old basis and 2026-10-02 on the new, so the provider rebuilt the series between 2026-09-05 and 2026-10-03. 2026-08-28 is on the new basis too, from the same Saturday fetch that returned the active silver contract. One of the 104, 2026-03-27, is the same contract (equal volume) restated by 0.50.
gold_series_rebuilt.resolution: Panel left as written; no correction. Neither series is wrong, and 104 corrections would be 104 full copies of the panel. But the panel now mixes the two, so a GOLD change measured from an old-basis week to a new-basis one includes that week's spread, 0.01 to 1.67 percent: d1w across 2026-08-21..08-28 reads -2.0 percent where the same contract fell 3.2, and every d4w, d13w and d52w that ends after 2026-09-04 and starts on or before it is off the same way. Which contract month GOLD means, and how it rolls, is a decision about the instrument and has not been made.

silver_active_contract_settlement.what: SILVER for 2026-08-28 is the December contract's settlement, not the front month's.
silver_active_contract_settlement.evidence: 67.786 on 85,735 contracts is SIZ26.CMX's row for the date (67.786 on 87,627). The provider's SI=F history carries 66.995 on 4,329. It is the same Saturday fetch that had no Friday bars for the index symbols: at 14:10 UTC the provider's history for the 28th was not yet in its final form.
silver_active_contract_settlement.resolution: Not corrected, in the original or in 2026-08-28.corrected.json. Both numbers are settlements for the date; which contract month SILVER means is the same undecided question as GOLD.

evening_last_trade.what: A futures or dollar-index close read on the evening of the session: the last trade, not the settlement.
evening_last_trade.evidence: The weekly files for 2026-09-11, 09-18 and 09-25, fetched at 19:51, 22:40 and 18:14 ET on the Friday, and the daily files for the first two. Same contract as the settled history (volumes within 7 percent); the close is off by 0.03 to 0.06 on WTI, 0.70 to 18.90 on GOLD and 0.005 to 0.065 on DXY.
evening_last_trade.resolution: Panel left as written. The writer no longer reads CL=F, GC=F, SI=F, 2YY=F or DX-Y.NYB before 13:00 UTC on the day after as_of, and truth_check --feed fails a file dated 2026-10-05 or later that carries one read earlier. The weekly job has to run on Saturday morning for the file to have them at all.

evening_quote_other_contract.what: A futures close read on the evening of the session, from a different contract month than the settled history.
evening_quote_other_contract.evidence: WTI 2026-09-18: 95.47 on 300,567 contracts is CLX26 (November), which settled 96.08 on 317,767. The history's close for the date is 100.30 on 112,698: CLV26 (October), two sessions from expiry (issue #110 recorded both contracts' prices that Saturday). This is its 95.47 against 100.30. SILVER 2026-09-11, 09-18 and 09-25: 65.02, 66.785 and 64.71 on 36,000 to 53,000 contracts are SIZ26 (December), which settled 65.188, 67.149 and 64.801; the history carries the front month on 49 to 526 contracts. The live quote of a continuous symbol follows the most active contract; the history does not.
evening_quote_other_contract.resolution: Panel left as written, and guarded as above. Not corrected: no sign-off was asked for these. Issue #110 asked for the WTI bar to be restated; scripts/restate_instruments.py would set it to the provider's 100.30 in one command, but 100.30 (October) and 96.08 (November) are both settlements for that date, and choosing is the undecided question above.

next_session_quote.what: A daily file's futures and dollar-index closes are the first trades of the NEXT session.
next_session_quote.evidence: The six Monday-to-Thursday daily files written between 19:41 and 19:59 ET (2026-09-14 to 09-17, 09-22, 09-23). Globex reopens at 18:00 ET and the provider stamps the live bar with the calendar date, so 'the bar dated as_of' at that hour is the new session: WTI on 593 to 2,923 contracts against 265,972 to 422,683 settled. 2026-09-22 holds WTI 89.63 against 94.59, SILVER 67.955 against 65.932, and 2026-09-16 GOLD 4308.50 against 4387.50.
next_session_quote.resolution: Panel left as written, and guarded as above: at the daily job's hour these instruments are now listed in missing with the reason. sector-regime-heatmap reads fx.DXY from the daily files for one comparison row, which will show as missing until the daily job runs after settlement.

vix_window_opened_on_dst_sunday.what: VIX is absent from two weekly files.
vix_window_opened_on_dst_sunday.evidence: Both list it in missing with 'no data returned for window 2025-03-09..' and '2026-03-08..'. Those are the Sundays US clocks went forward, and the provider returns no rows at all for ^VIX when a window opens on one (reproduced 2026-10-05; a window opening a day either side returns the whole week). Friday minus five days is that Sunday once a year. Cboe's history has 21.77 and 27.19 for the two Fridays.
vix_window_opened_on_dst_sunday.resolution: Panel left as written: the gaps are declared, which is the contract. The fetch window now opens on the week's Monday, so March 2027 is not a third. Filling the two weeks would be a correction that adds a close, which rebuild_corrections.py cannot re-apply and truth_check refuses.
